tasks.short: Choose economical transport routes and shipment consolidation options.

steps.what: Review shipments, delivery windows, loads and warehouse dispatch constraints.
Check contracted transport rates, carrier capacities and service restrictions.
Compare routes, consolidated loads and alternative distribution points.
Confirm unusual delivery constraints and carrier feasibility with dispatch.
Select routes and consolidation changes against cost, service and disruption risk.
Release the approved route plan to dispatch.
Compare actual transport cost and service with the selected plan.

tasks.design: Feed shipments and validated rate tables into the routing module of the {OPS_SYSTEM}; configure capacity, delivery-window and consolidation constraints. The manager reviews feasible scenarios before release to dispatch, and the {BI} compares planned cost and service with actual results.
tasks.previous_blocker: Routing tools can already optimise loads, but incomplete constraints and disconnected rate data leave managers comparing scenarios manually.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing optimisation software handles route search. AI-assisted coding makes rate imports, constraint validation and actual-versus-plan reporting cheaper to connect.
tasks.still_hard: Customer flexibility, carrier reliability and warehouse consolidation costs can be poorly recorded. Moving distribution capacity requires a separate investment decision.
tasks.human_edge: Judge when a cheaper route threatens service or creates an operational dependency.

ambition.what: Weekly flexible-delivery consolidation offers for small customers.

tasks.altitude: The manager reviews costed alternatives and spends less time rebuilding route comparisons. Route approval authority stays the same; a customer-facing consolidation service would need a separate commercial mandate.

reach.task: Validate route feasibility before dispatch release.
reach.learn: Delivery restrictions, loading sequences and driver-hours constraints.

reach.task: Evaluate alternative distribution points.
reach.learn: Network modelling, handling costs and sensitivity analysis.

evidence.claim: ORTEC provides route planning capabilities.
The Carrefour Poland sponsored case describes reducing kilometres per pallet through route planning.
Route scenarios can be generated by constrained optimisation without a language model.

assumptions: The existing {OPS_SYSTEM} includes a licensed routing module; otherwise deterministic optimisation needs a larger build.
Warehouse consolidation scenarios use existing sites and capacities, not automatic facility closures.
Only approved route plans are released internally; carrier booking follows existing authority.
GDPR applies where routes contain personal data. Individual driver allocation or monitoring requires separate EU AI Act assessment and applicable national consultation.
unknowns: Routing module availability and supported constraints.
Accuracy of dimensions, rates, delivery windows and address data.
Carrier booking responsibilities and dispatch approval rules.
Applicable employee consultation requirements.
research_questions: How much planned consolidation survives realistic warehouse and carrier constraints?
Which customers value flexible delivery enough to support a consolidation offer?
new_work: Maintain rate tables, delivery restrictions and routing constraints.
Investigate infeasible plans and actual-versus-plan variances.
Monitor optimisation runtime and mapping-data costs.
Develop commercial terms and capacity limits for any consolidation offer.
tasks.statement: Select transportation routes to maximize economy by combining shipments or consolidating warehousing and distribution.

tasks.short: Diagram supply chain flows for customer discussions.

steps.what: Agree the customer question, scope and level of detail.
Retrieve locations, stock movements and service constraints.
Reconcile location names and assemble the network table.
Draw locations, routes, handoffs and explanatory labels.
Check operational accuracy and approve the customer view.
Discuss the diagram and capture customer corrections or alternatives.

tasks.design: A reusable generator accepts exports from the {OPS_SYSTEM} and {ERP}, validates location mappings and renders a diagram in the {DOCS}. Start with file uploads; add scheduled retrieval through the {DATA_PLATFORM} where access permits. The manager approves the customer view and leads the discussion.
tasks.previous_blocker: Location identifiers differed, and each diagram was manually redrawn for its audience.
tasks.enabler_now: Established graph layout libraries and reusable data mappings make generation practical. AI coding can shorten connector and template development; no model is needed during normal use.
tasks.still_hard: Records omit informal handoffs, temporary routes and commercially sensitive details. Choosing the right abstraction remains contextual.
tasks.human_edge: Understand what the customer is worried about and explain the operational tradeoffs honestly.

ambition.what: Customer route-change comparison showing the current network beside one proposed alternative.

tasks.altitude: The manager spends less time drawing and more time testing customer alternatives. No new commercial approval rights are assumed.

reach.task: Validate route and throughput assumptions for customer scenarios.
reach.learn: Network data modelling, flow reconciliation and clear visual explanation.

evidence.claim: Structured network tables can drive repeatable diagrams with deterministic layout and validation.
Customer framing and approval of commercially sensitive diagrams remain human work.

assumptions: The first release covers one network and a small set of diagram templates.
Stable location identifiers or an approved mapping can be supplied.
The diagram represents operations; it does not claim to optimise the network.
GDPR applies if extracts contain personal data; customer diagrams exclude unnecessary personal fields.
unknowns: Which exports and read permissions are available?
How much reconciliation and redrawing occurs today?
Who approves disclosure of routes, capacities and supplier locations?
Do national rules require consultation for the proposed data use?
research_questions: Can template layouts remain legible across typical network sizes?
Which missing-data checks prevent misleading customer diagrams?
new_work: Resolve unmapped locations and missing route endpoints.
Maintain mappings and diagram templates.
Review generated diagrams before customer use.
Check connector changes and data freshness.
tasks.statement: Diagram supply chain models to help facilitate discussions with customers.

tasks.short: Negotiate supplier and freight terms, secure approval, and record the agreement.

steps.what: Collect spend, volumes, service failures, and current supplier terms.
Compare rate sheets, contract clauses, alternatives, and expected demand.

loop.input: Supplier contracts and quotations, alongside structured spend and demand fields.
loop.output: Cited rate and clause fields for a deterministically calculated negotiation brief.
loop.check: Validate currencies, units, effective dates, and totals; show source passages for every extracted clause.
loop.stop: At most 20 documents and two extraction passes per brief; unresolved fields go to manual review.
loop.why_not_simpler: Calculations are deterministic, but supplier wording and document layouts vary.

steps.what: Approve target terms, walk-away limits, and escalation boundaries.
Negotiate price, capacity, service commitments, and concessions with the supplier.
Turn agreed deal notes into a contract draft and proposed rate table.

loop.input: Recorded deal notes, approved templates, and the negotiation mandate.
loop.output: Contract draft and proposed rate fields, with deviations highlighted.
loop.check: Match commercial fields to deal notes; flag missing agreement and departures from approved clauses.
loop.stop: One draft and one correction pass; unresolved terms remain blank for the procurement specialist.
loop.why_not_simpler: Template fields are deterministic, but negotiated qualifications arrive in free text.

steps.what: Review legal deviations and reconcile the contract with negotiated commercial terms.
Approve and sign the agreed contract through the signature process.
Enter signed commercial terms and effective dates into purchasing records.

tasks.design: Configured exports from the {ERP}, {PROCUREMENT}, and {OPS_SYSTEM} feed a negotiation brief; bounded extraction adds cited terms from the {CLM}. A bounded drafting step prepares contract paperwork, while people negotiate, review deviations, and sign through the {ESIGN}. After signature, a configured flow publishes the reviewed rate table to the {PROCUREMENT}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Commercial evidence was split across transactions, rate sheets, and contracts. Relationships and negotiated exceptions made end-to-end automation unattractive.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing exports and signature workflows handle structured work. AI-assisted coding lowers the cost of connecting them, while bounded extraction handles varied documents.
tasks.still_hard: Supplier leverage, credible alternatives, capacity promises, and ambiguous concessions require commercial judgement. Contract mapping and access can dominate implementation cost.
tasks.human_edge: Read the supplier's incentives, trade concessions, protect trust, and decide when to walk away.

ambition.what: Structured renewal preparation for smaller suppliers previously receiving only reactive negotiation.

tasks.altitude: The manager spends less time assembling evidence and rewriting agreements, with more time testing alternatives before negotiations. Decision rights do not change automatically; mandates and signing limits still govern commitments.

reach.task: Calculate shipment-level cost-to-serve before freight negotiations.
reach.learn: Tariff structures, shipment characteristics, accessorial charges, and service-cost trade-offs.

evidence.claim: Structured commercial comparisons and publication of approved rates can use deterministic rules.
Transporeon checks freight invoices against agreed rates; this supports rate validation, not negotiation judgement.
A reported Pactum supplier-negotiation case demonstrates automation in a bounded commercial setting; it does not establish suitability for strategic negotiations.

assumptions: Estimates cover one purchasing category and a limited contract-template set.
Use existing reporting and workflow configuration before building connectors.
Supplier communications during negotiation remain human; no autonomous agent is needed.
Apply GDPR controls to supplier contact data and restrict access to confidential commercial records.
unknowns: Available exports, interfaces, and signature-trigger capabilities.
Contract-template quality and the proportion of bespoke clauses.
Delegated negotiation limits, legal-review thresholds, and signing authority.
Applicable national consultation requirements and access lead times.
research_questions: Which contract fields can be extracted reliably on representative redacted documents?
Can reviewed rate fields be published without rekeying after signature?
Which renewals lack adequate preparation today?
new_work: Review extracted clauses and missing commercial fields.
Resolve discrepancies between deal notes, contract wording, and rate tables.
Maintain templates, field mappings, and signature-trigger rules.
tasks.statement: Negotiate prices and terms with suppliers, vendors, or freight forwarders.

tasks.short: Review supplier performance, discuss forecasts, and agree improvement actions.

steps.what: Retrieve supplier delivery, shortage, and quality records from the {OPS_SYSTEM}.
Retrieve purchase commitments and material forecasts from the {ERP}.
Reconcile exports and calculate supplier measures in the {SPREADSHEET}.
Prepare the supplier review pack in the {DOCS}.
Discuss performance, challenge explanations, and negotiate recovery actions with the supplier.
Turn meeting notes into minutes and an action log in the {DOCS}.

loop.input: Manager's meeting notes and proposed commitments.
loop.output: Draft minutes and actions with owners, dates, and supporting note references.
loop.check: Check names and dates; distinguish proposals from agreements; manager checks disputed wording.
loop.stop: One extraction and one correction pass per meeting; unresolved statements remain flagged for manual editing.
loop.why_not_simpler: Free-text notes express commitments inconsistently; templates cannot reliably identify agreement.

steps.what: Approve and send supplier minutes through {EMAIL}, confirming commitments and follow-up dates.

tasks.design: Scheduled integrations join {OPS_SYSTEM} performance records with {ERP} commitments on the {DATA_PLATFORM}, feeding a {BI} scorecard and a templated review pack in the {DOCS}. A bounded loop turns manager notes into draft actions; a configured {WORKFLOW} sends the approved follow-up through {EMAIL} and tracks due dates.
tasks.previous_blocker: Supplier identifiers and metric definitions differ across records. Meeting outcomes arrive as informal notes.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing exports, reusable joins, document templates, and faster coding lower implementation effort. A bounded extraction loop handles the notes.
tasks.still_hard: Disputed delivery measures, confidential forecasts, and supplier leverage still require judgement. GDPR applies to named contacts and meeting records.
tasks.human_edge: Read hesitation, distinguish excuses from genuine constraints, and negotiate commitments the supplier can meet.

ambition.what: Weekly recovery-plan adjustments for critical suppliers.

tasks.altitude: The manager spends less time rebuilding packs and more time testing recovery commitments. Existing commercial authority remains unchanged; more frequent interventions fit within that authority.

reach.task: Estimate the transport and inventory cost of a supplier recovery proposal.
reach.learn: Cost-to-serve modelling, expedite costs, and uncertainty ranges.

evidence.claim: Structured supplier measures, templated packs, and reminders can use deterministic technology; the conversation remains human.
The proposed effort shares, remaining time, and build ranges are planning estimates, not measured results.

assumptions: Today, operational records and forecasts are reconciled in a workbook before supplier meetings.
Shares estimate active task effort, including preparation and follow-up; they exclude waiting.
The design uses manager notes and does not require meeting recording.
Access estimates cover supplier-contact data review and national consultation requirements where applicable.
unknowns: Which supplier identifiers and delivery definitions are authoritative?
Which forecast details may be disclosed to each supplier?
Who may commit to changed quantities, dates, or commercial terms?
Which exports, interfaces, and approval features are available?
research_questions: Does the existing {PROCUREMENT} already provide suitable scorecards and action tracking?
Can disputed deliveries be traced to receipt-level evidence?
How accurately can note extraction distinguish proposed and accepted commitments?
new_work: Resolve unmatched suppliers and disputed metric records.
Review extracted commitments before external sending.
Maintain metric definitions, connector mappings, and reminder rules.
tasks.statement: Meet with suppliers to discuss performance metrics, to provide performance feedback, or to discuss production forecasts or changes.

tasks.short: Document supply chain workflows, cycle times, responsibilities and system flows.

steps.what: Agree the process scope, intended readers and responsible process owner.
Observe physical work and ask operators about handoffs, exceptions and actual responsibilities.
Export relevant transactions and timestamps from the {OPS_SYSTEM}.
Calculate cycle times and distinguish processing, waiting and missing timestamps.
Draw process flows and write responsibilities, system handoffs and exception instructions.

loop.input: Scoped observation notes, validated cycle-time figures and existing procedure sections.
loop.output: Draft process graph, responsibility table and procedure with source references and unresolved gaps.
loop.check: Validate graph structure, references, role names and exact reuse of calculated figures; flag unsupported transitions.
loop.stop: One draft and one repair pass per process; unresolved roles or transitions remain marked for the walkthrough.
loop.why_not_simpler: Observation notes describe varied sequences and exceptions in prose; diagram rendering and numerical tables remain deterministic.

steps.what: Walk through the draft with operators and correct missing steps or disputed responsibilities.
Approve and publish the controlled procedure with its owner and review date.

tasks.design: A deterministic service on the {DATA_PLATFORM} reads scoped events from the {OPS_SYSTEM} and calculates cycle-time tables. A bounded drafting loop combines those tables with observation notes, then a deterministic renderer produces diagrams and procedures in {DOCS}. Configured document approval and versioning publish the procedure after an operator walkthrough and process-owner approval.
tasks.previous_blocker: Physical observations and transaction logs rarely formed one consistent record. Writing, drawing and maintaining documents required substantial manual effort even when the underlying process was understood.
tasks.enabler_now: Bounded drafting can turn notes into a structured first version, while ordinary code calculates metrics and renders diagrams. Existing document controls handle approval and versioning.
tasks.still_hard: Event logs show recorded transactions, not every physical step or actual responsibility. Undocumented workarounds require observation; worker-identifiable logs need GDPR controls and assessment under national rules.
tasks.human_edge: Discovering what people actually do and resolving disagreement about handoffs, responsibility and safe exceptions.

ambition.what: A verified process handover pack for temporary warehouse teams

tasks.altitude: The manager spends less time formatting procedures and more time observing work and resolving unclear handoffs. They can take responsibility for cross-team documentation readiness; operational change authority does not automatically change.

reach.task: Map process variation and identify bottlenecks.
reach.learn: Event definitions, observation methods and separating measured delay from incomplete logging.

reach.task: Validate receipt, movement and inventory exception instructions.
reach.learn: Frontline transaction sequences, practical checks and common workarounds.

evidence.claim: Event calculations, diagram rendering and document publication can use deterministic code and existing configuration.
A bounded drafting loop can structure observation notes, but operator validation is needed before treating the result as the actual process.
The digest provides no documented case establishing the proposed documentation savings.
Worker-identifiable operational logs require GDPR controls; employee consultation requirements depend on national rules and the intended use.

assumptions: The first release covers one process with accessible transaction timestamps.
Step shares, remaining time and build ranges are planning estimates.
Observation notes are collected directly; recording and transcription are outside the initial scope.
The consultation and access range includes event-data access and any required consultation about worker-identifiable logs.
Calculated metrics describe process performance rather than individual worker rankings.
unknowns: Whether timestamps reflect physical activity or delayed data entry.
Availability of stable transaction identifiers and event definitions.
Current document approval and version-control capabilities.
Whether observation notes or logs contain personal data.
Applicable national rules and employee consultation arrangements.
research_questions: Which physical steps are absent from transaction records?
Which timing measures remain reliable after missing and delayed entries are excluded?
Can each generated transition and responsibility be traced to an observation or approved source?
What operational changes should trigger a procedure review?

Review generated drafts with operators.
Maintain event definitions, templates and diagram checks.
Track procedure ownership, review dates and superseded versions.
Maintain data minimisation and access rules for operational logs.
tasks.statement: Document physical supply chain processes, such as workflows, cycle times, position responsibilities, or system flows.

tasks.short: Develop and implement supplier evaluation and selection procedures.

steps.what: Export supplier delivery, quality and purchasing performance from the {PROCUREMENT}.
Review supplier questionnaires, certificates and audit findings for usable evaluation evidence.

loop.input: Supplier questionnaires, certificates and audit reports, linked to supplier identifiers.
loop.output: Proposed evidence fields with document references, expiry dates and explicit missing values.
loop.check: Validate field types, supplier identity and dates; require a source passage and reviewer acceptance for material fields.
loop.stop: One extraction and one repair pass per document; unreadable, conflicting or unsupported fields enter the exception queue.
loop.why_not_simpler: Narrative audit findings and varying document layouts require interpretation; structured questionnaire fields use direct mapping.

steps.what: Agree evaluation criteria, weights, disqualifiers and exception responsibilities with stakeholders.
Build the supplier scorecard and its scoring formulas.
Test the method against previous awards, missing evidence and alternative weights.
Approve the evaluation policy, escalation thresholds and required award approvals.
Configure evaluation forms, scoring rules and approval routing in the {PROCUREMENT}.
Review pilot recommendations and decide whether the evaluation method needs changes.

tasks.design: Configure supplier forms, deterministic scoring and approval routing in the {PROCUREMENT}, with a bounded extraction loop for narrative evidence held in {DOCS}. A service on the {DATA_PLATFORM} generates scorecards and sensitivity tests, with results shown in {BI}. People approve criteria, material evidence and policy changes; supplier awards retain their required approval.
tasks.previous_blocker: Evidence was scattered across supplier documents and performance exports. Scorecards were easy to create but hard to validate, version and connect to approval processes.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing evaluation configuration handles structured criteria and routing. Deterministic generators and bounded document extraction can reduce assembly work while preserving evidence references.
tasks.still_hard: Weights encode business priorities and can conceal weak evidence. Historical awards are comparison cases, not proof of the correct decision; new suppliers may lack comparable performance data.
tasks.human_edge: Judging strategic dependence, credible improvement plans and risks that a weighted score cannot settle.

ambition.what: An evidence-based qualification route for small suppliers without delivery history

tasks.altitude: The manager spends less time constructing scorecards and more time challenging evidence and testing selection rules. They can gain authority to sponsor a controlled qualification route for new suppliers, while award authority remains with the designated approver.

reach.task: Validate supplier quality evidence and qualification thresholds.
reach.learn: Audit evidence, certificate scope and the difference between missing evidence and failed requirements.

reach.task: Test score sensitivity and compare alternative evaluation methods.
reach.learn: Weight sensitivity, missing-data treatment and validation without copying historical biases.

evidence.claim: Configured evaluation forms, deterministic scoring and sensitivity tests can support supplier-method design without autonomous selection.
Bounded extraction can propose fields from supplier documents, with source checks and human acceptance for material evidence.
The digest contains no direct case proving this supplier evaluation design or its estimated time savings.

assumptions: The first release covers one purchasing category.
Step shares, remaining time and build ranges are planning estimates.
The installed {PROCUREMENT} supports configurable evaluation forms and approval routing.
The consultation and access range includes confidential-document access, GDPR review for personal data and national consultation where applicable.
unknowns: Where delivery and quality performance records are actually held.
Which evaluation functions are licensed and available in the {PROCUREMENT}.
Existing procurement approval limits and mandatory qualification requirements.
Supplier document quality, languages and permitted reuse.
Applicable national rules and employee consultation arrangements.
research_questions: Which criteria are genuine disqualifiers rather than weighted preferences?
How sensitive are rankings to weights, missing evidence and uncertain measurements?
Which document fields can use direct mapping instead of a model loop?
How should new suppliers demonstrate capability without historical performance?
new_work: Review extracted evidence and conflicting supplier claims.
Maintain criteria versions, scoring rules and approval routes.
Investigate unstable rankings and recurring overrides.
Review certificate expiry and evidence freshness.
Maintain document access controls and extraction checks.
tasks.statement: Develop or implement procedures or systems to evaluate or select suppliers.

tasks.short: Design and implement warehouse strategies for production materials and finished goods.

steps.what: Export inventory, movement and location records for warehouse planning.
Walk the warehouse with supervisors to verify constraints and handling problems.
Compare storage, replenishment and picking options against capacity, service and cost.
Discuss operational tradeoffs with warehouse, production and safety representatives.
Write the investment request, pilot scope and rollout milestones.
Approve investment, operational disruption and pilot limits.
Set pilot locations, replenishment parameters and handling rules in the {OPS_SYSTEM}.
Review pilot results and decide whether to expand, change or stop.

tasks.design: A scheduled integration on the {DATA_PLATFORM} reads the {OPS_SYSTEM}, checks data quality and calculates warehouse scenarios using explicit capacity and cost constraints. A template generator produces the rollout proposal in {DOCS}, while configured pilot controls in the {OPS_SYSTEM} feed a results dashboard in {BI}. People verify physical constraints, choose the strategy and approve operational changes.
tasks.previous_blocker: Movement data, physical constraints and cost assumptions were maintained separately. Bespoke scenario calculations and connections were costly to build and maintain.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing exports, planning configuration and deterministic optimisation cover much of the preparation. AI coding can reduce implementation effort without changing the underlying planning methods.
tasks.still_hard: Congestion, safe handling and disruption during change need site knowledge. Inaccurate movement records or unrealistic assumptions can make a mathematically sound scenario impractical.
tasks.human_edge: Recognising unsafe or unworkable layouts and balancing service, investment and disruption with the people running the warehouse.

ambition.what: Monthly warehouse capacity and slotting adjustment decisions

tasks.altitude: The manager spends less time assembling comparisons and more time testing operational choices on site. They can gain delegated authority to adjust slotting within approved capacity, safety and spending limits.

reach.task: Build and validate warehouse capacity scenarios.
reach.learn: Constraint modelling, sensitivity analysis and validation against observed warehouse performance.

reach.task: Assess how material replenishment changes affect production schedules.
reach.learn: Production sequencing, material availability and replenishment lead times.

evidence.claim: Inventory planning software can calculate forecasts and stock settings; this supports replenishment analysis, not complete warehouse strategy design.
Lasaulec reported stock reductions above 20% and availability above 98%; the vendor case does not establish the same result for warehouse redesign.
Deterministic scenario calculations and template generation can reduce preparation while physical feasibility and investment decisions remain human.

assumptions: The first release covers one warehouse and existing handling equipment.
Step shares, remaining time and build ranges are planning estimates, not measured outcomes.
The consultation and access range includes a national-rules assessment and employee consultation if operational changes require it.
Capacity modelling uses aggregate operational data rather than individual worker scoring.
unknowns: Availability and quality of movement timestamps, dimensions and location capacities.
Supported exports and configuration interfaces in the installed {OPS_SYSTEM}.
Local approval limits for investment and warehouse changes.
Applicable national rules and existing employee consultation arrangements.
research_questions: Which existing planning functions can replace custom scenario code?
How well do historical scenarios reproduce observed congestion and service levels?
Which physical constraints must be recorded before a scenario can be considered feasible?
new_work: Maintain capacity, handling-cost and safety constraints.
Resolve missing dimensions and inconsistent movement records.
Check pilot outcomes against scenario assumptions.
Maintain integrations and review proposed configuration changes.
tasks.statement: Design or implement plant warehousing strategies for production materials or finished products.

tasks.short: Agree demand forecasts and feasible supply plans with planners.

steps.what: Assemble demand history, open orders, stock positions and supply commitments.
Prepare forecast adjustments and supply scenarios against capacity and lead-time constraints.
Discuss demand changes, shortages and scenario assumptions with planners.
Choose service priorities, forecast overrides and the feasible supply plan.
Record the approved plan and overrides in operational planning records.

tasks.design: A reusable planning view imports files or joins {ERP}, {OPS_SYSTEM} and {CRM} through {DATA_PLATFORM}. Configure available forecasting and constraint features in {OPS_SYSTEM}, expose exceptions in {BI}, and write back only the approved planning version with recorded override reasons.
tasks.previous_blocker: Snapshots used different cut-off times and planners reconciled scenarios by hand. Demand shifts and scarce capacity still required discussion.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing forecasting features can supply baselines, while cheaper adapters and validation code make a shared planning snapshot easier to build.
tasks.still_hard: Promotions, new products and uncertain supplier commitments weaken forecasts. Capacity models can omit real production constraints.
tasks.human_edge: Challenge commercial optimism, interpret weak signals and negotiate which customers or products receive scarce supply.

ambition.what: Daily shortage-priority decisions between scheduled planning meetings.

tasks.altitude: Planners arrive with checked scenarios, so the manager spends meetings on assumptions and allocation choices. Existing approval limits remain; faster evidence supports decisions within those limits.

reach.task: Check that the approved supply plan can become an executable production schedule.
reach.learn: Capacity calendars, material dependencies and frozen scheduling periods.

reach.task: Backtest forecasts and examine service effects of overrides.
reach.learn: Forecast bias, stockout-censored demand and override evaluation.

evidence.claim: Slim4 forecasts demand and sets stock by item and location.
Shared snapshots, constraint checks and approved-plan write-back can use deterministic technology.

assumptions: The first release covers one product family and planning horizon.
The target planning module supports baseline forecasts and the required basic constraints.
Spreadsheet scenario work is a typical cross-system bridge, although some companies already perform it in {OPS_SYSTEM}.
Plan release changes internal planning records; purchase orders and customer promises follow separate authorization.
No individual worker scoring is introduced.

Who can approve allocation changes and forecast overrides?

How should scenario evaluation account for demand hidden by stockouts?

Maintain capacity constraints and lead-time assumptions.
Review forecast bias and the effects of overrides.
Check that write-back preserves approval status and planning versions.

tasks.short: Define supply chain metrics, calculation rules and targets for cost, quality and service.

steps.what: Agree which business decisions and supply chain outcomes the metrics must support.
Inspect available fields, data coverage and existing calculations.
Specify formulas, denominators, exclusions, reporting grain, owners and proposed targets.
Backtest candidate metrics and examine sensitivity, missing data and misleading incentives.
Approve metric definitions and targets with affected operational owners.
Publish approved definitions and update dashboard calculations.

tasks.design: Keep versioned metric definitions in a records app on the {WORKFLOW}, linked to governed fields on the {DATA_PLATFORM}. Deterministic checks generate coverage and sensitivity reports; after approval, validated definitions update the catalogue and calculations in the {BI}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Definitions live in documents while calculations live elsewhere. Repeated data checks consume analyst time, but agreement on meaningful measures remains a management responsibility.
tasks.enabler_now: AI-assisted coding reduces the cost of a metric registry, reusable validation routines and controlled publication. No model loop is needed for explicit formulas and templates.
tasks.still_hard: Choosing fair comparisons, defensible exclusions and useful targets remains difficult. A precise metric can still reward the wrong behaviour.
tasks.human_edge: Choose measures that reflect real service and cost trade-offs, and challenge incentives that encourage gaming.

ambition.what: Monthly service-versus-working-capital target reviews.

tasks.altitude: The manager spends less time checking calculation consistency and more time discussing trade-offs and incentives. Metric approval rights remain unchanged; target reviews can use fresh evidence each month.

reach.task: Test whether proposed metrics support the intended decisions.
reach.learn: Measurement validity, sensitivity analysis and incentive effects.

reach.task: Define comparable quality measures across suppliers and sites.
reach.learn: Defect taxonomies, sampling limits and denominator consistency.

evidence.claim: Metric registries, formula checks and backtesting can use deterministic software.
Defining useful metrics requires judgement beyond automating dashboard production.
Build ranges assume a limited initial metric catalogue and accessible historical data.

The initial build uses an explicit formula vocabulary and a limited set of governed datasets.
GDPR applies wherever personal data enters the datasets. Extending metrics to employee evaluation requires separate EU AI Act assessment and consultation under applicable national rules.
The high automation prior is reduced because defining measures and agreeing targets remain substantial parts of this task.

Historical data quality and comparability across sites.
Who approves targets that affect other functions.
Whether any proposed metrics evaluate identifiable workers.

Which exclusions or denominators create unstable comparisons or incentives to game results?

Maintain field lineage, formula versions and historical comparability.
Investigate data drift and unintended incentives.
Retire measures that no longer support a named decision.
tasks.statement: Define performance metrics for measurement, comparison, or evaluation of supply chain factors, such as product cost or quality.

tasks.short: Analyze inventory and choose actions that balance turns, waste and customer service.

steps.what: Extract stock, demand, movements and inventory valuation at a common cut-off.
Reconcile item codes, units, valuation differences and missing movement records.
Calculate turns, ageing, service levels and alternative stock-policy outcomes.
Validate apparent excesses and shortages with warehouse and planning teams.
Choose stock-policy changes and assign excess-stock or service-recovery actions.
Review whether assigned actions improve stock, waste and service measures.

tasks.design: A reusable calculator starts with inventory file imports, then joins {OPS_SYSTEM} and {ERP} in {DATA_PLATFORM} with explicit reconciliation rules. A {BI} dashboard shows ageing, service trade-offs and stock-policy scenarios; {WORKFLOW} tracks approved actions and subsequent results.
tasks.previous_blocker: Inventory and financial records used different definitions and cut-offs. Repeat analysis required manual joins, while the reasons behind exceptional stock remained local knowledge.
tasks.enabler_now: Deterministic calculations and configurable inventory features already exist. AI-assisted coding makes reusable mappings, reconciliation checks and scenario views cheaper to assemble.
tasks.still_hard: Recorded demand can hide lost sales, and high turns can accompany poor availability. Obsolete stock, strategic buffers and unreliable suppliers need contextual judgement.
tasks.human_edge: Distinguish unnecessary stock from deliberate resilience and balance cash release against customer harm.

ambition.what: Daily prioritization of slow-moving-stock interventions.

tasks.altitude: The week shifts from reconciling reports toward choosing interventions and checking their effects. The manager gains a stronger basis for recommendations; write-offs and policy changes remain within existing approval limits.

reach.task: Investigate stock discrepancies before they influence policy recommendations.
reach.learn: Cycle-count controls, stock status codes and movement reconciliation.

reach.task: Evaluate inventory-policy alternatives against service and working-capital outcomes.
reach.learn: Demand segmentation, safety-stock assumptions and comparable outcome measures.

evidence.claim: Slim4 supports forecasts and stock settings by item and location.
The Lasaulec vendor case reports stock falling over 20% with availability above 98%; the period is unspecified.
Reconciliation, ageing metrics and stock-policy scenarios can be calculated deterministically; local outcomes require validation.

assumptions: The first release covers one inventory scope with agreed metric definitions.
No case-study result is treated as a forecast of customer savings.
Recommendations do not automatically dispose of stock, release purchases or change customer commitments.
Data access follows GDPR requirements where records contain personal data.
Access estimates include required reviews; national consultation requirements depend on the actual deployment.

Are quarantine, consignment and reserved stock identified consistently?

tasks.short: Forecast material costs and maintain approved standard cost lists.

steps.what: Export purchase prices, material usage and existing standards from the {ERP}.
Read supplier quotations and price notices received through the {EMAIL}.

loop.input: Supplier quotations and price notices, including attachments.
loop.output: Draft rates with currency, unit, validity, quantity breaks and source references.
loop.check: Validate required fields and arithmetic; review changed rates and ambiguous commercial terms.
loop.stop: One extraction and one repair pass; ambiguous or incomplete rates remain excluded.
loop.why_not_simpler: Suppliers use inconsistent documents and describe price conditions in free text.

steps.what: Normalise currencies, units, freight and duties in the {SPREADSHEET}.

Calculate material forecasts, proposed standards and changes from current costs.

tasks.design: Configured extracts from the {ERP} feed a versioned cost calculator on the {DATA_PLATFORM}; a bounded loop turns quotations from the {EMAIL} into reviewable rate records. Deterministic calculations produce forecasts, sensitivities and proposed standards, with assumptions visible in the {BI}. The {WORKFLOW} records finance approval and releases only that approved version to the {ERP}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Supplier formats varied, unit conversions lived in individual workbooks, and approval records were separate from uploaded costs.
tasks.enabler_now: Faster development lowers the cost of reusable conversion rules, source-linked quotation extraction and controlled publication. Standard costing functionality already exists in many {ERP} deployments.
tasks.still_hard: Future prices, yield losses and purchasing volumes remain uncertain. Finance must decide which assumptions are appropriate for official standards.
tasks.human_edge: Distinguish a temporary price movement from a lasting cost change and challenge commercially weak assumptions.

tasks.altitude: The manager spends less time rebuilding cost lists and more time testing price and yield exposure. They can recommend purchasing responses within existing authority; finance retains approval of official standards.

tasks.short: Assess supplier manufacturing capability through visits, observations and measured evidence.

steps.what: Arrange the supplier visit, attendees and evidence request through the {EMAIL}.
Prepare the assessment brief from supplier records and submitted documents.

loop.input: Supplier dossier, previous findings and approved assessment checklist.
loop.output: Brief with evidence references, outstanding questions and proposed verification points.
loop.check: Require a source for factual statements; assessor checks coverage and visit priorities.
loop.stop: One draft and one revision; unsupported statements become questions.
loop.why_not_simpler: Supplier narratives and previous findings contain context that fixed fields do not capture.

steps.what: Observe production, question staff and witness capability measurements at the supplier site.
Compile measured capacity, quality results and checklist completion in the {SPREADSHEET}.
Challenge findings and judge sustainable capacity, process control and delivery risk.
Write the capability assessment and proposed qualification conditions.

loop.input: Recorded observations, measurements, assessor judgement and required corrective actions.
loop.output: Draft assessment separating observed evidence, supplier claims and assessor conclusions.
loop.check: Reconcile figures to measurements; assessor verifies every finding and qualification condition.
loop.stop: One draft and one correction pass; unresolved evidence stays explicitly unresolved.
loop.why_not_simpler: A useful report must explain contextual observations and the assessor's reasoning.

steps.what: Approve the assessment and qualification status in the {PROCUREMENT}.

tasks.design: The {WORKFLOW} prepares visit logistics and a structured assessment record, while bounded loops draft the brief and report from evidence in the {DOCS}. Configured forms calculate measurement summaries and flag missing evidence; the assessor conducts the visit and makes the capability judgement. The quality manager approves qualification status in the {PROCUREMENT}.
tasks.previous_blocker: The essential evidence comes from physical observation and questioning. Preparation and reporting also relied on disconnected documents and repeated transcription.
tasks.enabler_now: Configured assessment forms and source-linked drafting can reduce paperwork around the visit. They do not replace direct observation or establish that supplier claims are true.
tasks.still_hard: A visit may show a staged or unrepresentative process. Assessors must judge sustained capacity, challenge explanations and follow up corrective actions.
tasks.human_edge: Notice inconsistencies on site, ask revealing follow-up questions and judge whether observed performance can be sustained.
tasks.altitude: Visits and capability decisions remain central to the week. Less preparation and report writing creates more time to verify corrective actions; decision rights do not change.

reach.task: Verify closure of supplier corrective actions.
reach.learn: Root-cause evidence, representative sampling and effectiveness checks.

reach.task: Use qualified supplier capacity in production plans.
reach.learn: Demonstrated capacity, utilisation limits and qualification conditions.

evidence.claim: Assessment forms, completeness checks and measurement summaries can use existing configuration.
Drafting support can reduce assessment paperwork while physical observation and capability judgement stay human.

assumptions: The assessment includes a physical supplier visit and an existing qualification checklist.
Time shares describe active assessment effort and exclude travel and waiting.

Visit communications require approval because access arrangements and confidentiality terms vary.
